title: The Promises and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence for Teachers: a Systematic Review of Research
extended_summary:
This paper systematically reviews empirical research on how teachers use artificial intelligence (AI) applications and machine-learning methods in education. The authors were motivated by the fact that AI is increasingly present in education, but teachers’ perspectives, roles, and needs have been less examined than student-facing applications. Their review asks what kinds of data are collected from teachers, what roles teachers play in AI-based research, what benefits AI offers teachers, what challenges arise, and which AI methods are most commonly used.

The review searched Web of Science for English-language journal articles published over the previous 20 years and identified 44 empirical studies focused on in-service K-12 teachers and pre-service teachers. The studies covered a range of AI uses, including automated scoring, predictive models of teacher outcomes, classroom monitoring, adaptive feedback, and tools informed by teacher data. Teachers appeared in several roles, such as models for training AI, providers of performance data, sources of student information, and evaluators of assessment systems.

The authors conclude that AI is most often reported as helping teachers with planning, implementation, and assessment by identifying student needs, supporting timely monitoring and feedback, and reducing workload. However, they also identify major challenges, including limited reliability, limited technical capacity, infrastructure constraints, context-specificity, and slow or insufficiently adaptive feedback. They argue that more research is needed on pre-service teachers, multimodal data, and deeper teacher involvement in AI system design.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review, but it does not present a new causal evaluation or pooled effect estimate for the focal comparison. The review synthesizes observational and design studies, so the evidence quality for the specific teacher-facing AI coaching/feedback question remains indirect and correlational/qualitative overall.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests practical promise for AI in teachers’ planning, monitoring, and assessment, but it reports no effect sizes for lesson quality, feedback usefulness, revision quality, uptake of feedback, or planning speed. Its contribution is mainly conceptual and descriptive rather than demonstrating measurable impact on the requested outcomes.
